narration.headline: different properties: correlation -0.0172 across 25 cells; no other statistic between them is returned
narration.framing: model-vs-model agreement (no ground truth), not accuracy

result.method: pointwise pixel-value sampled on a grid over the shared extent (an estimate, not every pixel); windows where either map is no-data are dropped before any statistic; no ground truth, so this is model-vs-model agreement (no ground truth), not accuracy.
result.warning: the results measure different properties (['sample_karst_score', 'sample_number']), so their values are different quantities: only the correlation (whether they rise and fall together) is meaningful, and it is the only statistic returned between them. A mean difference, an RMSE, an agreement fraction or an ensemble spread would mix two quantities, so none is computed; do not work one out, and do not say one reads higher than the other.
result.sampling_note: the 6x6 grid has 36 cells; each of the 2 results was sampled once per cell, so 72 samples were requested; 25 compared, 11 dropped (no-data or failed in either map; n_nodata_dropped and n_failed_dropped count those cells)
result.nodata_rule: a sample is no-data, and never enters a statistic, when its band is missing or NaN, equals the model's nodata_value, lies outside the band's declared regression range, or carries no class on a classification band

content:
Comparison done. Here's what I found:

**What the two models predict (per-pixel regression values, not confidences)**

| | KarstBinary result | KarstNumber result |
|---|---|---|
| Property | `sample_karst_score` (0–1) | `sample_number` (0.2–1.2) |
| Result id | `419c581d-…f26b` | `afb1cf68-…ae8` |
| Mean over shared extent | 0.10049 | 0.681763 |

**Where they differ**
- The two results measure *different quantities*, so only their correlation is meaningful: **correlation −0.0172** across the 25 comparable grid cells (of 36 sampled; 11 cells dropped as no-data in either map, over ~10,091 km² of shared extent). In practice the two maps do not agree in pattern at all — one reads high where the other reads low on average, and they rise/fall together essentially nowhere.

**Which one is right**
I can't tell you, and any answer would be made up: there are no ground-truth karst labels for this area, so neither map's accuracy is assessable, and mixing the two scales to call a winner isn't valid. Two honest next steps:

1. **If you have a reference karst map/labels**, I'll score both against it (per-window error rates, classification metrics).
2. **If you don't**, I can design a label plan (e.g., spend N window inspections via `olmoearth_plan_label_sample`) to estimate how wrong each map is before committing to one.

Want me to set up option 2?
